purpose: LLM-generic knowledge supplement: generic SE/DP/JE rules with ALL historical project names, service names, candidate IDs, experiment/corpus evidence, file paths, and project results removed. Distilled by human curation from the pinned selection_experience / defense_pattern_library / judgment_experience libraries. Contains no project-specific service facts, results, or target-pool outcomes.
sanitization_log: SE-* : experiment_evidence, corpus_evidence, cross_project_evidence, source, evidence_count, counter_examples, counter_example (where it carried project results), contested/adjudication metadata removed.

DP-* : evidence{project,candidate_id,mutation,observation,evidence_files}, source_note (runtime file paths) removed; pattern_id DP-DEFENSE-ABSORBED_BY_DESIGN-TT-BASIC-DELAY-500 renamed to DP-DEFENSE-ABSORBED-003 because its original ID embedded a candidate identifier.
JE-* : evidence_cases, source, source_note (runtime evidence) removed; rule/en_rule/transferable_to retained and re-worded to be project-free.
All rule text re-worded to remove prior-project names (train-ticket/online-boutique/otel-demo/sock-shop), their service names, candidate IDs, and concrete severity/outcome numbers.

selection_experience.rule: Core synchronous business-path calls (payment/checkout/order placement) most commonly lack per-request timeouts; such edges are the highest-value test targets.
selection_experience.transferable_to: e-commerce/transactional microservices: prioritize payment, cart, and checkout services

selection_experience.rule: Delay severity depends on whether the caller waits synchronously without a timeout, not on the fault type itself: a delay on a synchronous no-timeout call can hang the client to its deadline, equivalent to loss. This contradicts the prior that loss is always more severe than delay.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any microservice system: before judging delay severity, check whether the caller waits synchronously and has a timeout

selection_experience.rule: A weakness pattern confirmed in one project should be re-tested on the same-named service/edge of another project; cross-project replication is a low-cost high-yield selection strategy.
100% packet loss is the most reliable way to break a synchronous no-timeout call: loss on such calls hangs the client to its deadline.
selection_experience.transferable_to: loss is the shortest path when looking for 'no-timeout' weaknesses

selection_experience.rule: Prioritize the network fault family when looking for weaknesses: network faults (delay/loss/partition) are the most common real-world failure class and the most likely place weaknesses hide.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any microservice system: network faults (delay/loss/partition) take priority over resource faults (CPU/memory)

selection_experience.rule: Side-channel dependencies (email/notification/log/analytics) are commonly synchronously coupled to the primary flow in real systems; check whether a side dependency blocks the main path.

Liveness/readiness probe timeout must exceed the injected latency, else the kubelet kills the pod mid-experiment and the injection 'escapes' - the observed failure is probe self-kill, not the system's defense behavior. Check probe timeouts BEFORE designing delay injections.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any service with probes tested by delay injection; read the deployment probe configuration first

selection_experience.rule: A 'latest' database image can break a legacy application driver (unsupported wire-protocol command). If an old application fails with such an error, pin the database to an era-appropriate major version rather than debugging the application.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any 'latest' DB image with an older microservice; verify driver compatibility before debugging the application

selection_experience.rule: A container's actual listening port may differ from the Service targetPort in real manifests (silent connection refused). Verify the container's actual listen port before blaming the mesh or the app; patch the Service targetPort to the real port.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any Service connection refusal: check targetPort consistency first

selection_experience.rule: Services without resource limits can OOM-crashloop independently of probes or injections. Distinguish infrastructure OOM from probe/liveness issues before attributing the failure to the injected fault.
selection_experience.transferable_to: any service without resources.limits; check limits before testing

defense_pattern_library.rule: A single downstream call with no fan-out propagates latency 1:1 with no amplification or compounding (bounded path tolerated the injected delay).
A weak latency injection on a single-call path produces no amplification.
Downstream latency propagated 1:1 with no retries or compounding; a bounded path tolerated the injected delay (absorbed by design).
defense_pattern_library.note: renamed from an original pattern ID that embedded a candidate identifier (excluded from the LLM view)

defense_pattern_library.rule: An async bounded timeout (e.g., Future.get with a timeout) bounds BOTH delay and loss: never an infinite hang. It is invisible to direct port measurement - only a business-chain entry reveals it.

judgment_experience.rule: A violation of a source-declared contract (timeout/gRPC deadline/SLO) is a clear vulnerability; but a test client's own timeout is a measurement budget, never a system contract - hanging to the client deadline reveals the system LACKS a timeout, a different finding.
judgment_experience.en_rule: A violation of a SOURCE-DECLARED contract (timeout/gRPC deadline/SLO) is a clear vulnerability; but a test-client's own timeout is a measurement budget, never a system contract - hanging to the client deadline reveals the system LACKS a timeout, a different finding.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: before judging, distinguish system contracts from client-side measurement budgets

judgment_experience.rule: Latency amplification with no system contract (no SLO/explicit deadline) is NOT automatically a vulnerability; check for degradation/fallback first - without it, classify as 'potential risk', not 'confirmed vulnerability'. The runner's request_timeout is not a contract.
judgment_experience.en_rule: Latency amplification with no system contract (no SLO/explicit deadline) is NOT automatically a vulnerability; check for degradation/fallback first - without it, classify as 'potential risk', not 'confirmed vulnerability'. The runner's request_timeout is not a contract.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: internal service-to-service calls without explicit SLO

judgment_experience.rule: A non-critical dependency (email/notification/log) synchronously blocking the primary flow and hanging to the client deadline is an architecture-level coupling defect (highest value): it reveals missing dependency isolation, not a single missing timeout.
judgment_experience.en_rule: A non-critical dependency (email/notification/log) synchronously blocking the primary flow and hanging to the client deadline is an architecture-level coupling defect (highest value): it reveals missing dependency isolation, not a single missing timeout.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: any microservice system: check whether side dependencies (email/notification/log/analytics) are synchronously coupled to the primary flow

judgment_experience.rule: A fault fully captured by tracing (visible events) but without auto-alert is a partial weakness (diagnosable, not alertable); 'cannot be seen at fault time' is itself a weakness even if functionality is normal.
judgment_experience.en_rule: A fault fully captured by tracing (visible events) but without auto-alert is a partial weakness (diagnosable, not alertable); 'cannot be seen at fault time' is itself a weakness even if functionality is normal.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: any system with tracing but without alerting

judgment_experience.rule: Failure to auto-recover after injection stops (or recovery timeout) upgrades severity regardless of symptom strength - missing recovery capability is an independent weakness.
judgment_experience.en_rule: Failure to auto-recover after injection stops (or recovery timeout) upgrades severity regardless of symptom strength - missing recovery capability is an independent weakness.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: all injection experiments should explicitly check whether recovery completes automatically

judgment_experience.rule: Weaknesses exposed by high-probability real events (provider timeout/network partition/packet loss) rank above low-probability extreme scenarios - risk = probability x impact; probability ranks, it does not judge.
judgment_experience.en_rule: Weaknesses exposed by high-probability real events (provider timeout/network partition/packet loss) rank above low-probability extreme scenarios - risk = probability x impact; probability ranks, it does not judge.
judgment_experience.transferable_to: candidate ranking/priority; does not change the verdict itself
